newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Zealand's Sir Peter Blake to follow Cousteau.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's Sir Peter Blake to follow Cousteau.

text.p: New Zealand navigator Sir Peter Blake has been named to carry on the message of the late French oceanographer Jacques-Yves Cousteau, the Cousteau Society said on Saturday.
Following the death on June 25 of the 87-year-old Cousteau, who introduced the wonders of the sea to the world, his widow Francine was formally named head of the Cousteau Foundation.

"Sir Peter Blake, currently the head of the America's Cup winner Team New Zealand, will first participate in Cousteau's main projects as much as he can and lead the Cousteau Team full-time in two years after leading his country's defence of the America's Cup," the Society said in a statement.

"As a sailor, an adventurer, an environmentalist and a gentleman, Sir Peter is the perfect person to represent the Cousteau Society through its future explorations, discoveries and awareness of the planet," it said.
Blake plans to repeat New Zealand's 1995 victory in yachting's most prestigious trophy when it saw off Dennis Conner's Young America 5-0 in San Diego.
In the meantime, the Society said, it would gather the funds necessary to build Captain Cousteau's dream boat the Calypso II which will be ready in the year 2000.
"Following New Zealand's America's Cup defence Sir Peter Blake will enter the next millennium at the helm of Calypso II," it said.
